topic: Mixed: World Cuisines, 90s Hip Hop & R&B, Seafood, Women's Soccer, Minecraft

masthead.dek: World cuisines, 90s hip hop and R&B, seafood, women's soccer, and Minecraft — six questions each. Every answer comes from a list you can walk: countries, states, cities, years, counts. Narrow it down, place your bet, then tap to check.
masthead.footer_html: Verified to FIFA, NOAA Fisheries, FAO, Billboard, the Recording Academy, the World Instant Noodles Association, the Minecraft Wiki and others. Current-year figures are as of November 2026.

plan.note: Six questions per topic, interleaved. Answers rotate across countries, U.S. states, cities, years/decades, counts, groups, foods and Minecraft blocks/mobs.

questions.dimension: pasta eaten per person outside Europe
questions.q: Italians eat more pasta for each person than anyone else. Outside of Europe, which country's people eat the most pasta per person?
questions.detail: About 17 kg of pasta per person per year, second in the world behind Italy.
questions.why: Italy leads at roughly 23 kg per person, but the runner-up is not in Europe or the Americas: Tunisia, at about 17 kg, eats more pasta per head than Greece, the U.S., or Argentina.
questions.more: Venezuela is usually third at about 12 kg. Figures come from industry surveys of different years, so the exact kilograms vary by source, but Tunisia's second place is consistent.
questions.source: International Pasta Organisation figures as reported by World Grain (https://www.world-grain.com/articles/10423-global-pasta-consumption-continues-to-rise); Il Sole 24 Ore / Unione Italiana Food

questions.dimension: repeat holder of the weeks-at-no-1 record
questions.q: In the 1990s, one R&B group set or tied the record for the most weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 three separate times. Which group?
questions.detail: 'End of the Road' (13 weeks, 1992), 'I'll Make Love to You' (14 weeks, 1994) and 'One Sweet Day' with Mariah Carey (16 weeks, 1995-96).
questions.why: 'End of the Road' broke a record Elvis Presley had held since 1956 (11 weeks). The group then matched or beat the new mark twice more within four years.
questions.more: Whitney Houston's 'I Will Always Love You' took the record to 14 weeks in between, so 'I'll Make Love to You' tied rather than broke it. The 16-week mark stood alone until 2017 and was not beaten until 2019.
questions.source: Billboard Hot 100 chart history (https://www.billboard.com/artist/boyz-ii-men/chart-history/)

questions.dimension: top salmon-farming country in the southern hemisphere
questions.q: Which country in the Southern Hemisphere farms the most salmon?
questions.detail: About 760,000 tonnes of Atlantic salmon in 2023, second in the world.
questions.why: Salmon are not native to the Southern Hemisphere at all, yet Chile farms roughly a quarter of the world's supply, second only to Norway's 1.48 million tonnes.
questions.more: The other southern farmers, Australia (Tasmania) and New Zealand, are far smaller, at well under 100,000 tonnes each. Chile has been the world No. 2 since 1992.
questions.source: FAO GLOBEFISH salmon market reports (https://www.fao.org/in-action/globefish/); Kontali, as of 2023

questions.dimension: first country to win both men's and women's world cups
questions.q: Which was the first country to win both the men's World Cup and the Women's World Cup?
questions.detail: Completed the double by winning the 2003 Women's World Cup; the men had already won three times.
questions.why: For 20 years Germany was the only member of this club. The women then won again in 2007, making Germany the first to defend the women's title.
questions.more: Spain became the second country to do it in 2023 (men 2010, women 2023). Brazil, Italy, Argentina, France, England and Uruguay have men's titles only; the U.S., Norway and Japan have women's titles only.
questions.source: FIFA tournament archives (https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/womens/womensworldcup)

questions.dimension: minimum obsidian for a nether portal
questions.q: A Nether portal frame still works with its four corners left out. What is the smallest number of obsidian blocks you need to build one?
questions.detail: A 4-wide by 5-tall frame uses 14 blocks; drop the 4 corners and 10 remain.
questions.why: The portal opening must be at least 2 wide and 3 tall, so the frame needs 2 blocks top, 2 bottom and 3 on each side: 2+2+3+3 = 10.
questions.more: The largest allowed frame is 23 by 23 blocks. Ten obsidian is exactly what a 'bucket method' speedrunner casts from lava.
questions.source: Minecraft Wiki, 'Nether portal' (https://minecraft.wiki/w/Nether_portal)

questions.dimension: instant noodles eaten per person
questions.q: Which country eats the most instant noodles for each person in a year?
questions.detail: About 81 servings per person in 2024, just ahead of South Korea's 79.
questions.why: South Korea held the top spot every year from 2013 to 2020. Vietnam passed it in 2021 and has led since, by a margin of only about two servings a year in 2024.
questions.more: If you answered South Korea you were right until 2021. By total servings the leader is China (with Hong Kong), then Indonesia and India; Japan, where instant noodles were invented, is only around 47 per person.
questions.source: World Instant Noodles Association data, reported by The Korea Times, Oct 2025 (https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/society/20251009/koreans-per-capita-ramyeon-consumption-ranks-2nd-after-vietnam)

questions.dimension: home state of the first hip-hop album-of-the-year winner
questions.q: In the late 1990s, a hip-hop album won the Grammy for Album of the Year for the first time. The artist who made it grew up in which U.S. state?
questions.detail: Lauryn Hill, raised in South Orange, N.J., won for 'The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill' at the 1999 Grammys.
questions.why: Hill won 5 Grammys that night, then a record for a woman in a single ceremony, with her only solo studio album.
questions.more: The common wrong guess is Georgia: OutKast's 'Speakerboxxx/The Love Below' won the same award five years later, in 2004, and is often misremembered as the first.
questions.source: Recording Academy, 41st Annual Grammy Awards (https://www.grammy.com/awards/41st-annual-grammy-awards)

questions.dimension: state of the most valuable u.s. fishing port
questions.q: Each year one U.S. fishing port brings in a catch worth more money than any other port's. Which state is that port in?
questions.detail: New Bedford, top U.S. port by value for more than 20 years in a row (about $443 million in 2022).
questions.why: New Bedford wins on price, not weight: its boats land sea scallops, one of the most valuable catches per pound in the country.
questions.more: Alaska is the tempting answer. Dutch Harbor, Alaska has been No. 1 by weight for 26 straight years (mostly pollock), but its catch is worth less in total.
questions.source: NOAA Fisheries, Fisheries of the United States (https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/national/sustainable-fisheries/fisheries-united-states), 2022 data

questions.dimension: first european women's world cup champion
questions.q: Which was the first European country to win the Women's World Cup?
questions.detail: Won the second tournament, in 1995, beating Germany 2-0 in the final in Sweden.
questions.why: Norway had lost the very first final to the United States in 1991, then came back four years later to win it all.
questions.more: Germany did not win until 2003, and Sweden, the 1995 host, still never has. Norway also took Olympic gold in 2000.
questions.source: FIFA Women's World Cup 1995 archive (https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/womens/womensworldcup/sweden1995)

questions.dimension: mob with the most health in java edition
questions.q: In Minecraft: Java Edition, which mob has the most health?
questions.detail: 500 health points (250 hearts).
questions.why: The Warden, which is not even a boss, has more health than both bosses: the Wither has 300 and the Ender Dragon 200.
questions.more: In Bedrock Edition the answer flips: the Wither there has 600 health, more than the Warden's 500.
questions.source: Minecraft Wiki, 'Warden' and 'Health' (https://minecraft.wiki/w/Warden)

questions.dimension: country of sriracha's namesake town
questions.q: Sriracha hot sauce is named after a seaside town. Which country is that town in?
questions.detail: Si Racha, a coastal town in Chonburi Province, where the sauce style was first made.
questions.why: The famous rooster bottle is American: Huy Fong Foods was started in Los Angeles in 1980 by David Tran, a refugee from Vietnam, which makes both the U.S. and Vietnam strong wrong guesses.
questions.more: Thai sriracha is thinner and sweeter than the American version and is mostly served with seafood and omelets.
questions.source: Wikipedia, 'Sriracha' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriracha); Huy Fong Foods company history

questions.dimension: studio albums released in the notorious b.i.g.'s lifetime
questions.q: The Notorious B.I.G. is often ranked among the greatest rappers ever. How many of his studio albums came out while he was alive?
questions.detail: Only 'Ready to Die' (1994). 'Life After Death' was released on March 25, 1997, 16 days after he was killed.
questions.why: A whole legend rests on one album released in his lifetime; he was 24 when he died on March 9, 1997.
questions.more: 'Life After Death' went on to be certified Diamond (10 million+ units) in the U.S. Two more albums were built from leftover recordings in 1999 and 2005.
questions.source: RIAA Gold & Platinum database (https://www.riaa.com/gold-platinum/); Britannica, 'The Notorious B.I.G.'

questions.dimension: most-eaten seafood per person in the united states
questions.q: Which kind of seafood do Americans eat the most of, measured by weight for each person?
questions.detail: Roughly 5 pounds per person per year, well ahead of salmon (about 3) and canned tuna (about 2).
questions.why: Shrimp alone is about a quarter of all the seafood Americans eat, and nearly all of it is imported.
questions.more: Canned tuna was No. 1 through the 1990s (3.4 lb vs shrimp's 2.8 lb in 1998); shrimp passed it around 2001 and has led every year since.
questions.source: National Fisheries Institute annual Top 10 list, via SeafoodSource (https://www.seafoodsource.com/news/supply-trade/shrimp-still-dominating-american-seafood-preferences-according-to-nfi-annual-list)

questions.dimension: first women's world cup host country
questions.q: Which country hosted the first Women's World Cup?
questions.detail: Held in Guangdong province in November 1991, with 12 teams.
questions.why: Games lasted 80 minutes instead of 90, and the United States beat Norway 2-1 in the final in front of about 63,000 fans in Guangzhou.
questions.more: China was due to host again in 2003, but the SARS outbreak moved that tournament to the U.S.; China got the 2007 edition instead.
questions.source: FIFA Women's World Cup 1991 archive (https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/womens/womensworldcup/chinapr1991)

questions.dimension: block boats slide fastest on
questions.q: On which block does a boat slide the fastest?
questions.detail: A boat reaches about 72.7 blocks per second on blue ice.
questions.why: That is nearly twice the top speed on plain ice or packed ice (40 blocks per second) and about nine times a boat's speed on water (8).
questions.more: Blue ice is crafted from 9 packed ice, which is itself 9 ice, so each block of blue ice costs 81 ice. Ice-boat tunnels in the Nether are the fastest long-distance travel in survival.
questions.source: Minecraft Wiki, 'Boat' (https://minecraft.wiki/w/Boat)

questions.dimension: decade of the first michelin guide
questions.q: The Michelin Guide, known today for giving stars to restaurants, started as a free booklet from a tire company to get people driving. In which decade was the first one printed?
questions.detail: First published in 1900, when France had fewer than 3,000 cars.
questions.why: The guide is far older than its stars: the first star was awarded in 1926, and the one-to-three-star ladder came in 1931.
questions.more: About 35,000 copies of the first edition were given away, listing garages, hotels and how to change a tire. The 1920s and 1930s are the common wrong guesses because of the stars.
questions.source: Michelin Guide, 'History of the Michelin Guide' (https://guide.michelin.com/en/about-us)

questions.dimension: shared home city of no limit and cash money
questions.q: No Limit and Cash Money were two of the biggest rap labels of the late 1990s. Both were run from the same city. Which one?
questions.detail: Master P's No Limit and the Williams brothers' Cash Money were both New Orleans operations by the late 1990s.
questions.why: In 1998 alone No Limit released more than 20 albums, and Cash Money signed a distribution deal with Universal reported at $30 million.
questions.more: No Limit actually began in 1991 as a record shop in Richmond, California, before Master P moved it home to New Orleans. Atlanta, Houston and Memphis are the natural wrong guesses.
questions.source: Britannica and label histories; Wikipedia, 'No Limit Records' and 'Cash Money Records'

questions.dimension: main fish in imitation crab
questions.q: Imitation crab sticks contain little or no real crab. Which fish are they mostly made from?
questions.detail: The fish is minced into a paste called surimi, then shaped and colored to look like crab leg.
questions.why: Alaska pollock is the largest fishery in the United States by weight, around 3 billion pounds a year, and the same fish fills most fast-food fish sandwiches and fish sticks.
questions.more: Some surimi uses Pacific whiting or other white fish, but pollock is the standard. Cod is the common wrong guess; pollock is in the cod family.
questions.source: NOAA Fisheries species profile, 'Alaska Pollock' (https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/species/alaska-pollock)

questions.dimension: country of the all-time international goals leader
questions.q: One player has scored more goals for a national team than anyone else in soccer history, men or women. Which country did that player play for?
questions.detail: Christine Sinclair scored 190 goals for Canada between 2000 and 2023.
questions.why: Sinclair's 190 is far ahead of the men's record: Cristiano Ronaldo finished with 146 for Portugal.
questions.more: The United States is the close wrong guess: Abby Wambach scored 184 and Mia Hamm 158. Sinclair passed Wambach in January 2020.
questions.source: Canada Soccer player records (https://canadasoccer.com); UEFA for the men's record, as of Nov 2026

questions.dimension: year microsoft bought mojang
questions.q: Microsoft bought Mojang, the studio that makes Minecraft. In which year was the deal announced?
questions.detail: Announced September 15, 2014, for $2.5 billion.
questions.why: Minecraft's full release was only three years old (November 2011) when it sold for $2.5 billion; it has since passed 300 million copies sold, the most of any video game.
questions.more: Creator Markus 'Notch' Persson left the company when the sale closed in November 2014.
questions.source: Microsoft News Center, 'Minecraft to join Microsoft', Sept 15, 2014 (https://news.microsoft.com/2014/09/15/minecraft-to-join-microsoft/)

questions.dimension: country where msg was invented
questions.q: MSG is the flavor powder many people link with Chinese take-out. In which country was it invented?
questions.detail: Chemist Kikunae Ikeda isolated it from kelp broth in Tokyo in 1908 and named the taste 'umami'.
questions.why: It went on sale in 1909 under the brand Ajinomoto, decades before the phrase 'Chinese restaurant syndrome' appeared in 1968.
questions.more: China is the reflex guess because of the take-out link, and it is today's biggest producer and user of MSG, but it did not invent it.
questions.source: Ajinomoto Group history (https://www.ajinomoto.com/aboutus/history); Britannica, 'monosodium glutamate'

questions.dimension: year a rap song first topped the hot 100
questions.q: In which year did a song by a rapper first reach No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100?
questions.detail: Vanilla Ice's 'Ice Ice Baby' hit No. 1 on November 3, 1990.
questions.why: It took 11 years from the first rap hit: 'Rapper's Delight' reached only No. 36 in early 1980, and Run-DMC's 'Walk This Way' stalled at No. 4 in 1986.
questions.more: Definition caveat: Blondie's 'Rapture' reached No. 1 in 1981 and includes a rapped verse, but it is a rock band's single. If you count it, the answer is 1981.
questions.source: Billboard Hot 100 archive, chart dated Nov 3, 1990 (https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/1990-11-03/)

questions.dimension: months ruled out by the oyster r rule
questions.q: An old rule says to eat oysters only in months with the letter R in their name. How many months of the year does that rule leave out?
questions.detail: May, June, July and August.
questions.why: The rule is at least 400 years old in print (1599) and tracked the warm months, when unrefrigerated oysters spoiled faster and wild oysters are spawning and taste thin.
questions.more: Archaeologists found people on the Georgia coast were already avoiding summer oyster harvests about 4,000 years ago. Farmed, refrigerated oysters are sold year-round today.
questions.source: Florida Museum of Natural History, study in PLOS ONE, 2019 (https://www.floridamuseum.ufl.edu/science/oysters-r-months/)

questions.dimension: city of the record women's soccer crowd
questions.q: The biggest official crowd ever counted at a women's soccer match filled a stadium in which city?
questions.detail: 91,648 at Camp Nou for Barcelona vs Wolfsburg, April 22, 2022.
questions.why: It beat a record set in the same stadium just three weeks earlier (91,553 vs Real Madrid), by 95 people.
questions.more: The record for national teams is 90,185 at the 1999 World Cup final in Pasadena, California. An unofficial 1971 final in Mexico City is often estimated at over 100,000 but was never formally counted.
questions.source: Guinness World Records, 'Largest attendance at a women's football match' (https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/702274-largest-attendance-at-a-womens-football-soccer-match)

questions.dimension: real minutes in a minecraft day
questions.q: If you never sleep, how many real-world minutes does one full Minecraft day and night take?
questions.detail: A full cycle is 24,000 game ticks at 20 ticks per second, which is 1,200 seconds.
questions.why: Time in Minecraft runs 72 times faster than real life: daytime lasts 10 minutes, night about 7, with dusk and dawn filling the rest.
questions.more: A phantom appears after 3 in-game days without sleep, which is only one real hour of play.
questions.source: Minecraft Wiki, 'Daylight cycle' (https://minecraft.wiki/w/Daylight_cycle)

questions.dimension: yerba mate drunk per person
questions.q: Yerba mate is a strong leaf tea sipped through a metal straw across much of South America. Which country's people drink the most of it for each person?
questions.detail: Roughly 8 to 10 kg of yerba per person per year.
questions.why: Uruguay drinks about one and a half times as much per head as Argentina (about 6 kg), yet grows almost none of it and imports nearly all its supply from Brazil.
questions.more: Argentina is the biggest grower and the biggest drinker in total, so it is the natural wrong guess. Paraguay, where the plant is native, favors it cold as tereré.
questions.source: Statista per-capita yerba mate data (https://www.statista.com/statistics/884925/consumption-yerba-mate-per-capita-latin-america); Instituto Nacional de la Yerba Mate (Argentina)

questions.dimension: home state of missy elliott, timbaland and the neptunes
questions.q: Missy Elliott, Timbaland and the Neptunes shaped the sound of late-1990s hip hop and R&B. They all came from the same state. Which one?
questions.detail: All from the Hampton Roads area: Portsmouth (Elliott), Norfolk (Timbaland) and Virginia Beach (Pharrell Williams and Chad Hugo).
questions.why: Three of the era's most copied production sounds came from cities within about 20 miles of each other, far from the New York, Los Angeles and Atlanta scenes.
questions.more: Producer Teddy Riley moved his studio to Virginia Beach around 1990 and discovered the Neptunes at a school talent show there.
questions.source: Britannica biographies of Missy Elliott, Timbaland and Pharrell Williams (https://www.britannica.com/biography/Missy-Elliott)

questions.dimension: top caviar-producing country
questions.q: Which country produces the most caviar today?
questions.detail: More than half of the world's farmed caviar, by recent estimates.
questions.why: Wild Caspian sturgeon fishing collapsed and trade in wild caviar was restricted from 2006, so nearly all caviar is now farmed, and one Chinese firm, Kaluga Queen, is the largest single producer.
questions.more: Russia and Iran are the classic guesses from the Caspian era. Estimates of China's share range from about one-third to over 60% depending on year and source.
questions.source: China Daily citing the Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences, Jan 2026 (https://global.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202601/24/WS697420cea310d6866eb35859.html); EUMOFA caviar market study

questions.dimension: only women's world cup winner outside europe and north america
questions.q: Which is the only country from outside Europe and North America to win the Women's World Cup?
questions.detail: Won in 2011, beating the United States on penalties after a 2-2 draw.
questions.why: Japan had never beaten the U.S. in 25 earlier tries, and won four months after the 2011 earthquake and tsunami.
questions.more: Brazil is the tempting guess but has never won; its best is runner-up in 2007. China lost the 1999 final on penalties. Every other title belongs to the U.S. (4), Germany (2), Norway (1) or Spain (1).
questions.source: FIFA Women's World Cup 2011 archive (https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/womens/womensworldcup/germany2011)

questions.dimension: overworld ore found only in mountains
questions.q: Which Overworld ore can be found only in mountain biomes?
questions.detail: Emerald ore generates only in mountain-type biomes such as meadows, peaks and windswept hills.
questions.why: Unlike every other ore, emerald gets more common the higher you go, peaking near Y=236, and it usually appears as a single block rather than a vein.
questions.more: Diamond is the common wrong guess, but it generates under every biome. Most players get emeralds by trading with villagers instead of mining.
questions.source: Minecraft Wiki, 'Emerald Ore' (https://minecraft.wiki/w/Emerald_Ore)
